_comment: One job per STRIP — the whole strip as one image, for the concept run. Run with comic_render.py --provider runway|google|openai.

jobs.title: Tourist Season, 2002
jobs.prompt: a four-panel newspaper comic strip, four equal panels in a single horizontal row with thin black gutters (4 panels). Style: black and white comic strip panel, scratchy crow-quill pen and ballpoint ink on cardstock, harsh photocopy contrast, heavy black spotting, jagged uneven line weights, 1990s indie comix zine style, xerox grain, no color, no gray tones. Cast, the same faces, hair and builds in every panel, ages exactly as given: WOOD — aged 22, thin young man with a slouch, three days' stubble, dark hair grown longer; BARNABY (the dog) — a low-slung terrier and hound mix, long body, short legs, folded velvet ears, wiry white-and-tan coat, gray on the muzzle from 2004, cloudy eyes from 2009, carried from 2010. Clothes, hair-dos and anything held come from this strip's description, never from the reference sheet; hands are empty unless a panel names what they hold. Title of the strip: DRIFT WOOD. The strip: The seawall in August: tourists photographing the bay, Wood on the bench drawing them on a napkin, a tourist wanting to buy it. It's a napkin. He gives it away and draws another. Panel 1: a crowded seawall with tourists holding cameras and a young man on a bench drawing on a napkin with a small dog beneath it, brush-pen black and white (in this panel: WOOD, BARNABY (the dog)). No dialogue in this panel. Panel 2: a tourist in a sun hat leaning over a young man's shoulder to look at a napkin drawing, brush-pen black and white (in this panel: WOOD). Tourist says "How much?". Panel 3: a young man holding out a drawn-on paper napkin, brush-pen black and white (in this panel: WOOD). Wood says "It's a napkin.". Panel 4: a young man on a seawall bench beginning a new drawing on a fresh napkin with a small dog beneath the bench, brush-pen black and white (in this panel: WOOD, BARNABY (the dog)). No dialogue in this panel. Lettering: every balloon and caption contains its complete text exactly as written, in clean hand-lettered comic capitals, large enough to read; size each balloon to fit its whole sentence and never cut a word at a balloon or panel edge; no words other than the ones given. Bottom right margin: tiny signature "A. Finch — Small Wood, OR" beside a tiny stylized gull, two strokes. Reference @wood_20 is the model sheet for WOOD: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @barnaby is the model sheet for BARNABY (the dog): match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @loc_main_street shows the setting; keep its architecture and props. Match the attached references: @wood_20 for the character Wood at 20-23; @barnaby for the character Barnaby; @loc_main_street for the setting.
